recent_posts.title: Default value of appliesOnSubscription changed to true for app discount inputs
recent_posts.summary: Shopify has changed the default value of the `appliesOnSubscription` field from `false` to `true` on the `DiscountCodeAppInput` and `DiscountAutomaticAppInput` GraphQL Admin API input types. No action is required from developers — the change has no effect on checkout discount behavior, and apps that explicitly set this field are unaffected. The update applies across all active API versions.

recent_posts.title: Monitor admin web vitals in the Dev Dashboard
recent_posts.summary: Shopify has moved admin performance dashboards from the Partner Dashboard to the Dev Dashboard. Developers can now access daily and 28-day P75 rollups for three Core Web Vitals (LCP, INP, CLS) in one place. FID has been retired and replaced by INP. No code changes are required, and existing bookmarks will automatically redirect to the new location. The data shown matches what the App Store uses for Built for Shopify compliance evaluation.

recent_posts.title: Analytics metric targets now available in the GraphQL Admin API
recent_posts.summary: Shopify's GraphQL Admin API now supports analytics metric targets via four new operations: query, create, update, and delete. Merchants can set numeric goals for metrics like gross sales, track progress with visual gauges, and apps can read/write the same targets shown in the Shopify admin. Key features include deduplication by metric/date/filter, automatic status computation, and dimension-based filtering via ShopifyQL. Use cases include goal-setting apps, BI tools, planning apps, and agency dashboards. API version 2026-04 also adds two new ColumnDataType enum values for dimensionless scores and ratio/multiplier values.

recent_posts.title: Minor rounding change for custom line item discounts in POS 11.5
recent_posts.summary: Shopify POS 11.5 changes how fixed-amount custom line item discounts are calculated internally. Instead of applying the discount across the entire line, it will now be applied on a per-unit basis. This may cause rounding differences of up to one cent for amounts that don't divide evenly by quantity (e.g., a $5.00 discount on 3 items becomes $5.01). No action is required for extensions using API version 2026-04 or earlier, but a future API version will require passing per-unit discount amounts directly.

recent_posts.title: Scannable discount codes
recent_posts.summary: Shopify POS version 11.5 introduces scannable QR codes for discount codes. Merchants can generate QR codes from Shopify Admin that work at POS checkout and in online store sessions. No app changes are required, but developers who want to include QR codes as shareable links must replicate Shopify's URL-encoding format: simple codes encode directly, while special characters are double URL-encoded in the https://{shop}.myshopify.com/discount/{CODE} pattern.

recent_posts.title: Customer tax settings now available in Admin API
recent_posts.summary: Shopify's Admin GraphQL API version 2026-07 now exposes the taxSettings field on the Customer object publicly. Apps with the appropriate read customer data access scopes can query a customer's tax ID (e.g., VAT number) collected and validated during checkout. This is a read-only change returning the tax ID as a string or null. The validation status sub-field remains restricted to apps with approved protected customer data access. This aligns with existing B2B customer tax settings available since API version 2025-01.

recent_posts.title: Storefront Catalog MCP now implements UCP
recent_posts.summary: Shopify's Storefront Catalog MCP has been updated to implement UCP (Unified Catalog Protocol). Three new catalog tools are now available: `search_catalog` for filtered product searches with buyer context, `lookup_catalog` for batch product/variant lookups, and `get_product` for full product details with variant selection. The previous search and lookup tools are deprecated and will be removed on June 15th, 2026. Developers building with Storefront MCP tools must update tool names, endpoints, and request/response schemas to match the new UCP format.

recent_posts.title: Update to app uninstall reasons
recent_posts.summary: The app uninstall reasons shown to merchants in the Partner Dashboard have been updated to better reflect real-world uninstall motivations. The new options include: testing multiple apps, store closing or pausing, not using the app now, dissatisfaction with features or support, unexpected costs, and compatibility issues. These changes aim to give app developers clearer, more actionable data to improve their apps.

recent_posts.title: New app submission experience in the Partner Dashboard
recent_posts.summary: Shopify has updated the app submission experience in the Partner Dashboard with three key improvements: end-to-end review management with requirement-level tracking and structured fix workflows, an AI-powered self-review tool that checks apps against App Store requirements before submission, and expanded automated pre-submission checks. Apps currently in 'Reviewed' status continue through the existing email-based process, while apps in 'Submitted' status will receive feedback through the new dashboard experience once reviewed.

recent_posts.title: Removing deprecated PRIVATE and PUBLIC_READ enums on metaobject definitions
recent_posts.summary: Shopify is removing the deprecated PRIVATE and PUBLIC_READ enum values from the MetaobjectAdminAccess enum in the Admin GraphQL API as part of the 2026-07 release. These values are obsolete and never returned by the API. No code changes are required, but updating code is recommended to avoid ambiguity and potential access issues.
